official_skills.notes: angular-developer gives architectural guidance and idiomatic code; angular-new-app scaffolds via the Angular CLI. This is the broadest framework-team skill of the eight stacks - trust it and do not duplicate it.

gap_map.why_it_matters: angular-developer covers testing APIs, not which behavior deserves a test. API knowledge without strategy produces suites that test the framework rather than the product.
Angular workspaces grow into many libs. Nothing tells the agent when a folder should become a library, or when a shared lib has become a dumping ground.
gap_map.fallback: The mentor applies references/growth-signals.md with the stack thresholds below.

layers.name: unit
layers.belongs_here: services, pipes, guards, pure functions and business rules the style guide told you to move out of components
layers.signal_you_picked_wrong: the test builds a TestBed just to call one method

layers.name: component
layers.belongs_here: the template contract: what renders for given inputs, and what the component emits on user interaction
layers.does_not_belong_here: business rules that live in a service
layers.cost: moderate - needs TestBed and a fixture
layers.signal_you_picked_wrong: the test drives business branches by clicking

layers.name: integration
layers.belongs_here: a feature's components and services wired together, including routing

layers.name: e2e
layers.belongs_here: the handful of flows whose breakage is an incident

testing.proportions: No proportions stated by the Angular team. The style guide's separation rule sets the shape indirectly: logic pushed out of components is unit-testable, so most tests should be unit tests.
rules: Test files sit beside their subject and end in .spec.ts, matching the style guide's naming rule.
ng test must run with --watch=false in CI or the command never exits and the job hangs until it is killed.
If a rule needs TestBed to be tested, it is in the wrong place - the style guide says to move it out of the component first.
Read angular.json for the configured test builder before assuming a runner.
traps: A forgotten await fixture.whenStable() or fixture.detectChanges() makes an assertion run against the pre-change DOM, so the test passes on the old value.
Zone-based async tests using fakeAsync pass while the real app, running on a different change-detection path, does not.
Over-mocking the dependency graph in a component test means the test asserts the mocks, not the wiring it existed to check.
A test that subscribes without unsubscribing leaks between specs, so failures appear in an unrelated test file.
what_not_to_test: That a component is created - a test asserting only toBeTruthy() proves the constructor ran.
Framework behaviour: that @Input binds, that the router navigates.
Exact DOM structure. It changes on every template refactor.
testing.notes: Read angular.json for the configured test builder before assuming the runner. --watch=false is required in CI or the command never exits.

growth_thresholds.extract_component_library: >=3 occurrences of the same component across >=2 feature areas
growth_thresholds.extract_package: >=2 features import the same internal module - promote it to a workspace library
growth_thresholds.split_service: a service exceeds 5 injected dependencies, which usually means it owns more than one responsibility

layers.name: src/
layers.holds: all Angular UI code - TypeScript, HTML and styles - with the bootstrap in main.ts
layers.must_not: configuration files, which stay at the project root

layers.name: feature directory
layers.holds: everything one feature needs: its components, its services, its routes
layers.must_not: code a second feature also needs - that moves up, it does not get imported sideways

layers.name: component / directive
layers.holds: code relating to the UI shown on the page
layers.must_not: business logic, validation rules and data transformations - the style guide says to refactor those into separate functions or classes

variants.name: Feature directories (the style guide's recommendation)
variants.use_when: the default for any Angular app
variants.cost: you must decide per file whether something is shared, and that decision gets made badly under deadline

variants.name: Workspace libraries
variants.use_when: >=2 features import the same internal module, or separate teams own separate areas
variants.cost: build and release complexity, and boundaries you now have to maintain

variants.name: core/ + shared/ + features/ (community convention)
variants.use_when: a team already knows this layout and will keep it consistent
variants.cost: core/ and shared/ are type-based directories, which the official style guide advises against; shared/ in particular accumulates state and becomes a second app

rules: Group files by feature, not by type. The style guide explicitly advises against directories named components, directives or services.
All Angular UI code lives under src/, with the bootstrap in main.ts.
File names separate words with hyphens: a UserProfile component is user-profile.ts, and its test is user-profile.spec.ts.
Code in a component or directive relates to what is on the page. Business logic, validation and data transformation move into separate functions or classes.
A feature never imports from another feature. Shared behaviour moves up to something both inject.
Split a directory before it gets hard to navigate. The style guide sets no number; growth_thresholds does.
architecture.component_library: Promote to a shared location at >=3 occurrences across >=2 features. Anything promoted must be presentational: state in a shared component is how a shared folder turns into a second application.
architecture.notes: Verified against angular.dev/style-guide. The community core/shared/features layout is recorded as a variant, not as doctrine - the official guidance is feature grouping and it warns against type-based directories.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Angular ships signals and RxJS but takes no position above component state, so every app past a few screens picks something.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Signals plus plain services until an observable flow genuinely needs RxJS. NgRx when several unrelated features read and write the same state.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: It reaches every component and every test setup. Changing it later is a rewrite of the feature layer.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: Both work; the ecosystem moved to standalone but older codebases and tutorials use modules.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: A mixed codebase means two mental models and two ways to wire every dependency.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: The CLI supports both and neither is the default forever.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Single app until a second feature imports the same internal module.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Splitting late means untangling imports that grew across a boundary that was never enforced.

key_decisions.why_it_is_forced: SSR changes what code may touch the DOM, and retrofitting it surfaces every hidden browser assumption at once.
key_decisions.reasonable_default: Client only unless SEO or first-paint is a stated requirement.
key_decisions.cost_of_getting_it_wrong: Adding SSR later breaks every component that touched window or document directly.

operability.observability: An ErrorHandler provider is the single place an unhandled client error can be captured. Without one, errors reach the console and nowhere else.
operability.authorization: Guards decide route access, but they are UX. The control is on the server; a guard only decides what the user is shown.
done_checks: clean install from a fresh clone
rules: Every HttpClient call has a timeout and a stated retry policy. RxJS retry without a bound retries forever.
Loading affordance matches what you know: a progress bar with a percentage only for determinate work; a skeleton or spinner otherwise. Never a percentage you cannot compute.
An interceptor that swallows an error makes every downstream failure silent - it must rethrow or report.
Provide a custom ErrorHandler or unhandled errors are invisible outside the user's console.

Every asynchronous operation a user can see declares four states: loading, empty, error and success. Empty is not success with no rows, and success on a mutation is a confirmation, not a silent return to normal.
No secret in the client bundle. Everything in an Angular build ships to the browser.

dead_code_risks: Components referenced only from a route configuration
Providers resolved by injection token rather than by class import
Pipes and directives declared in a shared module and used only in templates
Public exports of a workspace library consumed by another library
Anything referenced only from a template string, which import-graph tools do not follow
